citation.authors: Meyer-Gerspach AC, Cajacob L, Riva D, et al.
citation.title: Mechanisms Regulating Insulin Response to Intragastric Glucose in Lean and Non-Diabetic Obese Subjects: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Parallel-Group Trial

population.description: 12 normal-weight (6 M, 6 F; age 24.3 ± 0.6 y, range 20-32; BMI 22.0 ± 0.4, range 19.0-24.9) and 12 non-diabetic obese (6 M, 6 F; age printed '29.4.8 ± 1.8' years, range 19-48, so the mean is unreadable and left null; BMI 38.8 ± 0.9, range 30.5-48.4) volunteers. Group ages and BMI are given on each arm; sd = SEM x sqrt(12) computed here (lean age 0.6 -> 2.08, lean BMI 0.4 -> 1.39, obese BMI 0.9 -> 3.12). The paper says 'all were healthy' and excluded smoking, drugs, illness (especially diabetes) and abnormal examination or laboratory screening. Lean arms are 'healthy' on that word; obese arms are 'unselected' because the paper itself finds them insulin resistant and hyperinsulinaemic (HOMA-IR 3.5, 'prediabetic factors') and gives a BMI range. After the 75 g load, one of the 24 subjects (group not stated) had impaired glucose tolerance and four (groups not stated) had a 60-min glucose above 8.6 mmol/L; none had diabetes. This classification was made after the test, not used to enrol. The paper reports no screening OGTT before enrolment.

protocols.name: lean_10g
protocols.description: lean group; 10 g glucose in 300 mL tap water instilled through a gastric (feeding) tube within 2 min (paper t = 0-2 min), tube then removed; dose and time are stated, entered as one carbohydrate meal at paper t = 0. Blood samples at t = -10 and -1 (fasting), 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180 min. Arm clock starts at the paper's t = -10 min, so the load is at arm minute 10 and the paper's t = 180 min is arm minute 190 (duration 191). Not stated: clock hour of the first sample (subjects were admitted at 08:00, tube and catheter placed after) and fasting hours ('at least 10 h' is a lower bound).
